answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a distinct geodetic survey vertex on a named hillside terrace, certified in person by a licensed surveyor who bolts a uniquely engraved copper tag to the marker. Random spot-checks summon the holder to photograph themselves beside that exact vertex within a day, and one person cannot be at two vertices at once. A registration fee in outside money doubles per vertex on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another terrace lease, another surveyor visit, another live human, and twice the prior fee.
